case_studies.title: Case-Specific Rubrics for Clinical AI Evaluation: Methodology, Validation, and LLM-Clinician Agreement Across 823 Encounters
case_studies.abstract: Objective. Clinical AI documentation systems require evaluation methodologies that are clinically valid, economically viable, and sensitive to iterative changes. Methods requiring expert review per scoring instance are too slow and expensive for safe, iterative deployment. We present a case-specific, clinician-authored rubric methodology for clinical AI evaluation and examine whether LLM-generated rubrics can approximate clinician agreement.   Materials and Methods. Twenty clinicians authored 1,646 rubrics for 823 clinical cases (736 real-world, 87 synthetic) across primary care, psychiatry, o
case_studies.summary: The study addresses the need for efficient evaluation methodologies for clinical AI documentation systems, proposing a case-specific, clinician-authored rubric approach. This approach leverages large language models (LLMs) to generate rubrics that approximate clinician agreement, aiming to reduce the time and cost associated with expert review. The methodology was tested across 823 clinical cases, demonstrating its potential for iterative deployment and safe implementation.
case_studies.how_to_apply: AI practitioners building clinical workflows can apply this methodology by engaging clinicians in the development of case-specific rubrics and leveraging LLMs to scale the evaluation process. This approach enables more efficient and cost-effective validation of clinical AI systems, facilitating their deployment and continuous improvement.
case_studies.monetisation: The proposed methodology unlocks business opportunities in the development of clinical AI evaluation tools and services, which can be marketed to healthcare organizations and technology vendors. By providing a scalable and cost-effective solution for clinical AI validation, companies can capitalize on the growing demand for reliable and safe clinical AI systems.

case_studies.title: Leveraging LLMs for Multi-File DSL Code Generation: An Industrial Case Study
case_studies.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) perform strongly on general-purpose code generation, yet their applicability to enterprise domain-specific languages (DSLs) remains underexplored, especially for repository-scale change generation spanning multiple files and folder structures from a single natural-language (NL) instruction. We report an industrial case study at BMW that adapts code-oriented LLMs to generate and modify project-root DSL artifacts for an Xtext-based DSL that drives downstream Java/TypeScript code generation. We develop an end-to-end pipeline for dataset construction, multi-file task r
case_studies.summary: The study addresses the challenge of generating and modifying domain-specific language (DSL) artifacts using large language models (LLMs) in an industrial setting. The researchers developed an end-to-end pipeline for dataset construction and multi-file task generation, adapting code-oriented LLMs for an Xtext-based DSL used at BMW. The outcome demonstrates the potential of LLMs in enterprise DSL code generation, with potential applications in various industries.
case_studies.how_to_apply: To apply this approach, AI practitioners should focus on constructing comprehensive datasets and developing adaptable pipelines for multi-file task generation, taking into account the specific requirements of their industry or use case. By leveraging code-oriented LLMs and fine-tuning them for their specific DSL, practitioners can unlock efficient and scalable code generation capabilities.
case_studies.monetisation: The study unlocks a concrete business opportunity for companies to develop and market AI-powered code generation tools tailored to specific industries or DSLs, potentially disrupting traditional software development workflows. By productizing this technology, companies can offer automated code generation solutions, reducing development time and costs for clients while generating significant revenue streams.
case_studies.relevance_tag: AI Agents, LLMs, Automation, NLP, MLOps

case_studies.title: Less Is More: Engineering Challenges of On-Device Small Language Model Integration in a Mobile Application
case_studies.abstract: On-device Small Language Models (SLMs) promise fully offline, private AI experiences for mobile users (no cloud dependency, no data leaving the device). But is this promise achievable in practice? This paper presents a longitudinal practitioner case study documenting the engineering challenges of integrating SLMs (Gemma 4 E2B, 2.6B parameters; Qwen3 0.6B, 600M parameters) into Palabrita, a production Android word-guessing game. Over a 5-day development sprint comprising 204 commits (~90 directly AI-related), the system underwent a radical transformation: from an ambitious design where the LLM
case_studies.summary: The problem of integrating Small Language Models (SLMs) into mobile applications is addressed in this paper, which presents a case study of incorporating SLMs into a production Android word-guessing game. The AI approach involved a 5-day development sprint with 204 commits to integrate two SLMs, Gemma 4 E2B and Qwen3, into the game. The outcome was a radical transformation of the system, achieving a fully offline, private AI experience for mobile users.
case_studies.how_to_apply: AI practitioners building workflows can apply the lesson of incremental integration and testing of SLMs to ensure seamless functionality and performance in their applications. By adopting a similar iterative development approach, practitioners can overcome the engineering challenges of on-device SLM integration and deliver private AI experiences to their users.
case_studies.monetisation: This research unlocks a concrete business opportunity for mobile application developers to create private, offline AI-powered experiences, enhancing user privacy and reducing cloud dependency. By leveraging SLMs, developers can create new revenue streams through premium features and subscription-based models that prioritize user data protection and privacy.

case_studies.title: FastOMOP: A Foundational Architecture for Reliable Agentic Real-World Evidence Generation on OMOP CDM data
case_studies.abstract: The Observational Medical Outcomes Partnership Common Data Model (OMOP CDM), maintained by the Observational Health Data Sciences and Informatics (OHDSI) collaboration, enabled the harmonisation of electronic health records data of nearly one billion patients in 83 countries. Yet generating real-world evidence (RWE) from these repositories remains a manual process requiring clinical, epidemiological and technical expertise. LLMs and multi-agent systems have shown promise for clinical tasks, but RWE automation exposes a fundamental challenge: agentic systems introduce emergent behaviours, coord
case_studies.summary: The Observational Medical Outcomes Partnership Common Data Model (OMOP CDM) has enabled the harmonisation of electronic health records data, but generating real-world evidence from these repositories remains a manual process. The proposed FastOMOP architecture utilises AI agents and LLMs to automate this process, addressing the challenges of emergent behaviours and coordination. This approach has the potential to improve the efficiency and accuracy of real-world evidence generation, enabling better clinical decision-making and healthcare outcomes.
case_studies.how_to_apply: To apply this approach, AI practitioners building workflows should focus on designing agentic systems that can adapt to the complexities of real-world data, while ensuring transparency and explainability in their decision-making processes. By leveraging multi-agent systems and LLMs, practitioners can develop more robust and reliable automation solutions for real-world evidence generation.
case_studies.monetisation: The FastOMOP architecture unlocks a significant business opportunity for companies developing healthcare AI solutions, as it enables the automation of real-world evidence generation and can be integrated into existing clinical workflows. This can lead to the creation of new products and services, such as AI-powered clinical trial design and real-world evidence analytics, which can be marketed to pharmaceutical companies, healthcare providers, and research institutions.
case_studies.relevance_tag: Healthcare AI, AI Agents, LLMs, Automation

case_studies.title: Personalized Worked Example Generation from Student Code Submissions using Pattern-based Knowledge Components
case_studies.abstract: Adaptive programming practice often relies on fixed libraries of worked examples and practice problems, which require substantial authoring effort and may not correspond well to the logical errors and partial solutions students produce while writing code. As a result, students may receive learning content that does not directly address the concepts they are working to understand, while instructors must either invest additional effort in expanding content libraries or accept a coarse level of personalization. We present an approach for knowledge-component (KC) guided educational content generat
case_studies.summary: The problem of adaptive programming practice is that it often relies on fixed libraries of worked examples and practice problems, which may not correspond well to the logical errors and partial solutions students produce. The AI approach presented is a knowledge-component guided educational content generation system that can create personalized worked examples from student code submissions. The outcome of this approach is a more personalized and effective learning experience for students.
case_studies.how_to_apply: AI practitioners building workflows can apply this approach by integrating knowledge-component guided educational content generation into their existing systems, allowing for more personalized and adaptive learning experiences. This can be achieved by leveraging pattern-based knowledge components to generate worked examples that cater to individual students' needs and learning styles.
case_studies.monetisation: This approach unlocks a concrete business opportunity for educational technology companies to develop and market personalized learning platforms that incorporate AI-generated worked examples and practice problems. By leveraging this technology, companies can create more effective and engaging learning experiences, leading to increased customer satisfaction and revenue growth.

case_studies.title: GradMAP: Gradient-Based Multi-Agent Proximal Learning for Grid-Edge Flexibility
case_studies.abstract: Coordinating large populations of grid-edge devices requires learning methods that remain fully decentralised in deployment while still respecting three-phase AC distribution-network physics. This paper proposes gradient-based multi-agent proximal learning (GradMAP) to address this challenge. GradMAP trains independent neural-network policies for each agent without any parameter sharing, and each agent uses only its own local observation for online decision-making without communication. During offline training, GradMAP embeds a differentiable three-phase AC power-flow model in a primal-dual le
case_studies.summary: The problem of coordinating large populations of grid-edge devices in a decentralised manner while respecting three-phase AC distribution-network physics is addressed in this paper. The proposed AI approach, GradMAP, uses gradient-based multi-agent proximal learning to train independent neural-network policies for each agent. This approach enables online decision-making without communication and embeds a differentiable three-phase AC power-flow model for offline training.
case_studies.how_to_apply: AI practitioners building workflows can apply the GradMAP approach by focusing on decentralised and independent agent learning, allowing for scalable and efficient decision-making in complex systems. By using gradient-based proximal learning, practitioners can develop methods that respect physical constraints and enable real-time decision-making.
case_studies.monetisation: The GradMAP approach unlocks concrete business opportunities in the energy sector, particularly in the development of intelligent grid-edge devices and smart grid management systems. By leveraging this technology, companies can create more efficient, scalable, and decentralised energy management solutions, leading to potential cost savings and revenue streams.

case_studies.title: Large-scale wireless network management via Open-RAN Tandem Apps: Cell on/off switching use case
case_studies.abstract: With growing mobile-network complexity, management and optimization have become increasingly difficult. Centralized algorithms face high control-data overhead and computational load, while distributed approaches often perform far from optimally. The O-RAN architecture introduces two tiers of RAN Intelligent Controllers (RICs), enabling hierarchical network-management schemes. This work proposes Tandem Apps: a pair of tightly coupled optimization mechanisms running on both controllers. We show how to design Tandem Apps through architectural and functional splitting to achieve an agile, low-comp
case_studies.summary: The increasing complexity of mobile networks makes management and optimization challenging, with centralized algorithms facing high overhead and distributed approaches performing suboptimally. This work proposes Tandem Apps, a pair of optimization mechanisms running on hierarchical RAN Intelligent Controllers, to achieve agile and low-complexity network management. The approach enables efficient cell on/off switching, but its practical implementation and outcomes are still theoretical.
case_studies.how_to_apply: AI practitioners building workflows can apply this concept by designing hierarchical control mechanisms that split optimization tasks between multiple controllers, allowing for more efficient and scalable network management. This approach can be adapted to various network optimization tasks, such as resource allocation and traffic management.
case_studies.monetisation: The proposed Tandem Apps approach unlocks a concrete business opportunity for telecom companies to develop and market more efficient network management solutions, potentially reducing operational costs and improving network performance. This can be achieved by integrating the Tandem Apps concept into existing network management systems or developing new products and services around this technology.

case_studies.title: Diffusion Templates: A Unified Plugin Framework for Controllable Diffusion
case_studies.abstract: Controllable diffusion methods have substantially expanded the practical utility of diffusion models, but they are typically developed as isolated, backbone-specific systems with incompatible training pipelines, parameter formats, and runtime hooks. This fragmentation makes it difficult to reuse infrastructure across tasks, transfer capabilities across backbones, or compose multiple controls within a single generation pipeline. We present Diffusion Templates, a unified and open plugin framework that decouples base-model inference from controllable capability injection. The framework is organiz
case_studies.summary: The problem of controllable diffusion methods being developed as isolated systems hinders their practical utility. The proposed AI approach, Diffusion Templates, is a unified plugin framework that decouples base-model inference from controllable capability injection. This framework enables the reuse of infrastructure across tasks and the composition of multiple controls within a single generation pipeline.
case_studies.how_to_apply: To build more flexible and adaptable workflows, AI practitioners can apply the concept of decoupling base-model inference from controllable capability injection. By using a unified plugin framework like Diffusion Templates, practitioners can more easily reuse infrastructure and compose multiple controls within a single generation pipeline.
case_studies.monetisation: The development of a unified plugin framework like Diffusion Templates unlocks business opportunities in the areas of AI model deployment and workflow optimization. Companies can leverage this technology to create more efficient and adaptable AI systems, leading to increased productivity and reduced development costs.

case_studies.title: Green Shielding: A User-Centric Approach Towards Trustworthy AI
case_studies.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed, yet their outputs can be highly sensitive to routine, non-adversarial variation in how users phrase queries, a gap not well addressed by existing red-teaming efforts. We propose Green Shielding, a user-centric agenda for building evidence-backed deployment guidance by characterizing how benign input variation shifts model behavior. We operationalize this agenda through the CUE criteria: benchmarks with authentic Context, reference standards and metrics that capture true Utility, and perturbations that reflect realistic variations in the E
case_studies.summary: The problem of large language models being sensitive to user query phrasing is addressed through a user-centric approach, which involves characterizing how benign input variation shifts model behavior. The proposed Green Shielding approach operationalizes this agenda through the CUE criteria, focusing on authentic context, utility, and realistic variations. The outcome of this approach is to provide evidence-backed deployment guidance for building trustworthy AI systems.
case_studies.how_to_apply: To apply this approach, AI practitioners can focus on developing benchmarks that capture realistic user interactions and behaviors, and prioritize the development of reference standards and metrics that reflect true utility. By doing so, they can identify potential pain points and areas for improvement in their AI systems, leading to more robust and reliable models.
case_studies.monetisation: The Green Shielding approach unlocks a concrete business opportunity for companies to develop and market AI systems that are specifically designed to be more robust and trustworthy, with a focus on user-centric design and real-world deployment scenarios. This could lead to the creation of new products or services that prioritize AI safety and reliability, such as AI auditing tools or AI deployment consulting services.

case_studies.title: Measuring Successful Cooperation in Human-AI Teamwork: Development and Validation of the Perceived Cooperativity and Teaming Perception Scales
case_studies.abstract: As human-AI cooperation becomes increasingly prevalent, reliable instruments for assessing the subjective quality of cooperative human-AI interaction are needed. We introduce two theoretically grounded scales: the Perceived Cooperativity Scale (PCS), grounded in joint activity theory, and the Teaming Perception Scale (TPS), grounded in evolutionary cooperation theory. The PCS captures an agent's perceived cooperative capability and practice within a single interaction sequence; the TPS captures the emergent sense of teaming arising from mutual contribution and support. Both scales were adapted
case_studies.summary: The problem of evaluating human-AI cooperation has become increasingly important as AI becomes more prevalent in various fields. To address this, the authors introduce two new scales, the Perceived Cooperativity Scale and the Teaming Perception Scale, which are grounded in joint activity theory and evolutionary cooperation theory. The outcome of this research provides a foundation for assessing the subjective quality of cooperative human-AI interaction.
case_studies.how_to_apply: AI practitioners building workflows can apply the lessons from this research by incorporating the Perceived Cooperativity Scale and the Teaming Perception Scale into their evaluation frameworks to assess the effectiveness of human-AI cooperation. By using these scales, practitioners can identify areas for improvement and optimize their workflows to enhance cooperative human-AI interaction.
case_studies.monetisation: The development of these scales unlocks a concrete business opportunity for companies to create products or services that evaluate and improve human-AI cooperation, such as AI-powered teaming tools or cooperative workflow optimization software. This can lead to increased efficiency and productivity in industries that rely on human-AI collaboration, such as healthcare, finance, or customer service.

case_studies.title: Joint Sato-Tate Laws for Transformations of Hecke Eigenvalues: The Vertical Case
case_studies.abstract: We introduce a framework within which a large class of joint equidistribution problems can be studied and resolved with effective error terms. This involves proving a higher dimensional and $μ$-analogue of the Erdös-Turán inequality, and utilizing the theory of the Hardy-Krause (H-K) variation from analysis, where, in particular, we formulate a technique to approximate a broad class of relevant functions by functions of bounded H-K variation. Our main focus will be on the vertical Sato-Tate problem for spaces of cusp forms and for families of elliptic curves over finite fields. In particular,
case_studies.summary: The problem addressed in this study is the joint equidistribution of Hecke eigenvalues for spaces of cusp forms and families of elliptic curves over finite fields. The AI approach involves proving a higher dimensional and μ-analogue of the Erdös-Turán inequality and utilizing the theory of the Hardy-Krause variation. The outcome is a framework for studying and resolving a large class of joint equidistribution problems with effective error terms.
case_studies.how_to_apply: To apply this research, AI practitioners building workflows can utilize the developed framework to study and resolve joint equidistribution problems in various mathematical contexts. By leveraging the theory of the Hardy-Krause variation, practitioners can approximate relevant functions and achieve effective error terms.
case_studies.monetisation: This research unlocks opportunities for developing advanced mathematical modeling tools and software for applications in cryptography, coding theory, and number theory. Potential business opportunities include creating products or services that utilize the developed framework for joint equidistribution problems, such as cryptographic protocol development or mathematical consulting services.

case_studies.title: Learning to Think from Multiple Thinkers
case_studies.abstract: We study learning with Chain-of-Thought (CoT) supervision from multiple thinkers, all of whom provide correct but possibly systematically different solutions, e.g., step-by-step solutions to math problems written by different thinkers, or step-by-step execution traces of different programs solving the same problem.   We consider classes that are computationally easy to learn using CoT supervision from a single thinker, but hard to learn with only end-result supervision, i.e., without CoT (Joshi et al. 2025). We establish that, under cryptographic assumptions, learning can be hard from CoT supe
case_studies.summary: The problem of learning from multiple thinkers is studied, where each thinker provides a correct but possibly different solution to a problem. The AI approach involves using Chain-of-Thought (CoT) supervision from multiple thinkers to learn a model. The outcome shows that learning can be hard from CoT supervision under cryptographic assumptions, highlighting the challenges of learning from diverse thinkers.
case_studies.how_to_apply: Practitioners building AI workflows can apply this lesson by considering the potential biases and differences in solutions provided by multiple thinkers, and designing their models to account for these variations. By doing so, they can develop more robust and generalizable models that can learn from diverse perspectives.
case_studies.monetisation: This research unlocks the potential for developing more advanced AI models that can learn from multiple thinkers, which can be applied to various industries such as education and healthcare. Companies can leverage this technology to create more effective and personalized learning systems, or to improve the accuracy of medical diagnoses by incorporating diverse expert opinions.

case_studies.title: Can Current Agents Close the Discovery-to-Application Gap? A Case Study in Minecraft
case_studies.abstract: Discovering causal regularities and applying them to build functional systems--the discovery-to-application loop--is a hallmark of general intelligence, yet evaluating this capacity has been hindered by the vast complexity gap between scientific discovery and real-world engineering. We introduce SciCrafter, a Minecraft-based benchmark that operationalizes this loop through parameterized redstone circuit tasks. Agents must ignite lamps in specified patterns (e.g., simultaneously or in timed sequences); scaling target parameters substantially increases construction complexity and required knowle
case_studies.summary: The problem of evaluating the capacity of agents to close the discovery-to-application gap is addressed through a Minecraft-based benchmark. The AI approach involves using parameterized redstone circuit tasks to operationalize the discovery-to-application loop. The outcome is the introduction of SciCrafter, a benchmark that can be used to assess the ability of agents to discover causal regularities and apply them to build functional systems.
case_studies.how_to_apply: Practitioners can apply this approach by using Minecraft or similar environments to test the ability of their agents to learn and apply causal regularities. By scaling target parameters, practitioners can increase the complexity of tasks and evaluate the limits of their agents' capabilities.
case_studies.monetisation: This research unlocks opportunities for developing more advanced AI agents that can be used in real-world applications, such as automation and robotics. Companies can leverage this technology to create more efficient and effective systems that can learn and adapt to new situations.

case_studies.title: Benchmarking Source-Sensitive Reasoning in Turkish: Humans and LLMs under Evidential Trust Manipulation
case_studies.abstract: This paper investigates whether source trustworthiness shapes Turkish evidential morphology and whether large language models (LLMs) track this sensitivity. We study the past-domain contrast between -DI and -mIs in controlled cloze contexts where the information source is overtly external, while only its perceived reliability is manipulated (High-Trust vs. Low-Trust). In a human production experiment, native speakers of Turkish show a robust trust effect: High-Trust contexts yield relatively more -DI, whereas Low-Trust contexts yield relatively more -mIs, with the pattern remaining stable acro
case_studies.summary: The study investigates how source trustworthiness affects Turkish evidential morphology and whether large language models track this sensitivity. It uses controlled cloze contexts to manipulate the perceived reliability of the information source and studies the past-domain contrast between -DI and -mIs. The results show a robust trust effect in human production experiments, with High-Trust contexts yielding more -DI and Low-Trust contexts yielding more -mIs.
case_studies.how_to_apply: AI practitioners building workflows can apply the findings of this study by considering the trustworthiness of information sources when designing language models, particularly in languages with evidential morphology like Turkish. By incorporating source trustworthiness into their models, practitioners can improve the accuracy and reliability of their language processing systems.
case_studies.monetisation: This study unlocks a concrete business opportunity in developing more accurate and reliable language processing systems, particularly in industries that require sensitive information handling such as finance or healthcare. Companies can leverage these findings to create more sophisticated language models that take into account the trustworthiness of information sources, leading to improved decision-making and risk assessment.

case_studies.title: Multiple positive solutions with prescribed masses for a coupled Schrödinger system: mass mixed and Sobolev critical coupled case
case_studies.abstract: The aim of this paper is to establish multiple positive normalized solutions $(u,v,λ_1,λ_2)\in H^1(\mathbb{R}^N,\mathbb{R}^2)\times \mathbb{R}^2$ to the following coupled Schrödinger system involving Sobolev critical exponent: $$ \begin{cases} -Δu+λ_1 u=μ_1|u|^{p-2}u+να|u|^{α-2}u|v|^β, x\in \mathbb{R}^N,\\ -Δv+λ_2 v=μ_2|v|^{q-2}v+νβ|v|^{β-2}v|u|^α, x\in \mathbb{R}^N,\\ \int_{\mathbb{R}^N}|u|^2\mathrm{d}x=a, \int_{\mathbb{R}^N}|v|^2\mathrm{d}x=b, \end{cases} N\geq 3, $$ where $μ_1,μ_2, ν, a, b>0$. We are particularly interested in the mass mixed case that $2<p, q<2+\frac{4}{N}, α>1, β>1$, and $
case_studies.summary: The problem addressed is the existence of multiple positive normalized solutions to a coupled Schrödinger system with prescribed masses. The AI approach involves mathematical modeling and analysis of the system, focusing on the mass mixed and Sobolev critical coupled case. The outcome is the establishment of multiple positive solutions to the system under certain conditions.
case_studies.how_to_apply: To apply this research, AI practitioners can utilize the mathematical frameworks and techniques presented in the study to analyze and solve similar problems in their workflows. By understanding the conditions and constraints that lead to multiple positive solutions, practitioners can develop more effective and efficient solutions to complex systems.
case_studies.monetisation: The research unlocks opportunities for the development of new products and services in fields such as quantum computing and materials science, where the analysis of complex systems is crucial. Companies can leverage the findings of this study to create innovative solutions and workflows that enable the discovery of new materials and phenomena.
